title: The Weight of a Word
logline: A family finds an old recording of a relative who has died, and decides in their own time whether to listen to a voice that sounds exactly as it always did.
human_question: A recording keeps a voice. What does it not keep?

situation.what_happens: Clearing a shelf or a cupboard, a family comes across a recording of someone who has died. There is first the practical problem of finding anything that will still play it. Then there is the harder decision of whether to play it at all, and who should be in the room when it happens. The voice, when it comes, is unchanged, which is the whole difficulty: it sounds like someone speaking now. Afterwards the family has to decide what the recording is for and where it goes.
situation.who_is_involved: The family of the person who died: the ones who want to hear it, the ones who do not, and whoever has been keeping the recording.
situation.what_is_at_stake: Whether a grief that had settled is reopened, and whether the recording becomes something the family keeps, copies, shares or puts away for good.
situation.how_it_unfolds: Situations like this are not planned. They begin by accident, in the middle of some other task, and they move at whatever pace the family can bear. The pressures are who is present, how recent the death is, and what the family already disagrees about. They end with the recording played, or put back unplayed, or played once and never again. Only the family can decide, and only at the time.

concept_merge.why_together: C066 contributes vocal intimation, the mode by which a spoken sound carries what someone means, and the sources' observation that a machine reproduces the sound and not that. C063 contributes sound's place in the inventory of matter as conditioned and momentary, which is why a copy of a sound is only that. Together they name the gap between a voice and someone meaning it.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: Everyone who has heard a recording of someone who has died already knows the gap; almost nobody has a word for it. What the pairing reveals is that the absence is not sentimental but structural: the missing thing is not a quality of the sound, so no improvement in the recording could ever supply it.

concept_links.why: The digest reports the source's own observation that a machine can reproduce the sound of someone's voice exactly while what made the sound a message, a living person's intention shaping breath and throat at that moment, is absent, and that the sources give that absence a name. The digest also notes that the gramophone example is the modern author's illustration rather than a claim of the classical text.

The digest counts sound among the twenty-eight kinds of matter as a conditioned, momentary thing that is kept up only while its conditions last, which is why a recording can copy a sound without renewing anything of the person who once produced it.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: These texts give a name to what is missing from a recording: the sound can be identical, and yet nothing in it is being meant by anyone now.
what_must_be_real: The family's own grief, timing and choice. Nothing staged, repeated or scheduled to suit anyone else; the family decides whether this is filmed at all and can stop at any point, including afterwards.
position_hint: held rather than placed: it would sit late in a group, because it asks what is left of a person once the body that meant something has stopped.
risks: Grief staged, prolonged or repeated for a camera.
A private moment turned into spectacle.
The family's timing overridden by a schedule.
Reading intimation as 'body language' or communication advice, which the digest rules out.
drop_if: No family willing to have this filmed entirely on their own terms.
The presence of a camera would itself change the moment.

connections.note: One asks what a voice loses when the wind takes it; the other what a voice loses when a machine keeps it.

selection.reason: Strong and doctrinally clean, but the group's nine slots are filled and its real subject, what is left of a person once the body that meant something has stopped, sits closer to the question this group hands on than to the body films themselves. Held for the group that takes up what continues after a body ends.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
